title: Kickoff-to-Commit: hosted API developer econ & activation notes
content:
Purpose
---------
Notes + quick experiments for messaging that take devs from first API call to committed paid usage. Focus = developer-first value props + simple quickstarts + pricing language that reduces churn and accelerates trials converting to small monthly commits. This is an operational playbook, not a final pitch deck.

Audience
---------
- Early-stage engineers and ML engineers building prototypes and feature pilots.
- Platform/infra folks evaluating performance/cost tradeoffs.
- Growth/product folks running activation funnels.

Principles (single-sentence north-star)
---------
Make the first API call feel like shipping: minimal friction, immediate measurable value, transparent cost signals.

Key developer-first value props (concise)
---------
1) Predictable latency at dev scale: "Hello world" in 200–500ms median so iterate fast locally and in staging.
2) Cost visibility by route/model: token + request breakdown surfaced immediately after first calls.
3) Seamless scale path: same API/rollout controls from sandbox -> reserved capacity with clear upgrade steps.
4) Opinionated defaults for cost/perf: batching, auto-cache, and a suggested quantized model for dev that is 3–5x cheaper.

Quickstart angles (3 distinct flows to test)
---------
A) 3-step microflow (for hackers): Sign up -> CLI key + curl example -> Hello response. Emphasis: 60s to first inference.
  - CTA microcopy: "Try a real inference in 60s — no card required"
  - Measure: time-to-first-successful-token, drop-off before creating key.

B) Feature-first microflow (for product-first teams): Template app (chat widget) repo + 1-click deploy -> real responses -> sample analytics. Emphasis: product signal > infra.
  - CTA microcopy: "Clone demo + ship a chat prototype in 5 minutes"
  - Measure: repo fork -> API key used in demo -> creation of project in Console.

C) Cost-aware pilot (for platform/infra): Guided trial with cost dashboard defaults + suggested commit options. Start with free credits, show projected monthly cost at 100k tokens/day.
  - CTA microcopy: "Estimate your monthly cost in 30s"
  - Measure: user opens cost estimator -> toggles model/batch settings -> requests pricing email.

Pricing-language experiments (3 variants)
---------
Variant 1 — Usage-first clarity (baseline)
  - Hero line: "Per-token pricing with transparent unit math"
  - Example microcopy: "Text-generation: $0.000X / 1k tokens (prompt + completion). We'll show a per-request cost breakdown after every call."
  - Experiment: show post-call receipt vs burying cost in billing page.

Variant 2 — Starter-credit + conversion funnel (growth experiment)
  - Hero line: "$50 starter credit + cost forecasts to go from prototype to pilot"
  - Microcopy for signup: "Start building—credit applied automatically. See a ‘projected monthly cost’ for your usage pattern."
  - Experiment: 50% of new signups get a proactive email estimating monthly cost for their first 10k tokens. Measure conversion.

Variant 3 — Commit-lite for teams (small reserved tiers)
  - Hero line: "Commit to save: small monthly reservations for predictable performance and price"
  - Offering: 50% discount on unit price for 1–3 month $500–$5k commitments; immediate SLA bump.
  - Microcopy in Console: "Recommended for teams running >50k tokens/day — save on cost and get dedicated capacity."

Competitive contrast (notes to use in copy/testing)
---------
- OpenAI: strong brand + experiments around simplicity. Weakness: limited observability and per-route cost controls in the same UI. Messaging: highlight our transparent per-route cost + rollout controls.
- AWS SageMaker / Endpoints: deep infra but higher friction for dev onboarding. Messaging: "No infra lift—same control plane when you need it."
- Self-hosted runtimes: lower unit costs at scale but longer time to iterate. Messaging: "Ship fast now — migrate to private/dedicated later without code changes."
- Lightweight inference providers (various): price-competitive but lack centralized evals/rollouts. Messaging: "Quality guardrails + monitored rollouts reduce surprise regressions."

Microcopy & snippets (pick-and-test)
---------
Signup page hero: "From hello-world to production: one API, one billing, fewer surprises."
Button: "Get started — build in 60s"
Email (after sign-up + starter credits): "You have $50 in credits. Make your first API call and we’ll show a per-request cost breakdown — try changing the model to see how cost/latency tradeoffs behave."
Console inline note near model selector: "Dev-friendy default: ‘gptx-dev-quant’ — 3x cheaper for experimentation. Swap to ‘gptx-prod’ for SLA-backed latency."
Billing receipt post-call: "This request: input 120 tokens + output 340 tokens = $0.00XX. Cumulative this session: 1,260 tokens ($0.00YY)."

A/B test ideas
---------
1) Show cost breakdown immediately after first call vs delayed 24h digest. KPI: conversion to paid usage within 7d.
2) Starter-credit with automated projected-cost email vs no email. KPI: activation -> commit rate.
3) Microcopy emphasizing "no card" vs "card optional" during signup. KPI: signup -> first call.

Measurement plan (minimum signals)
---------
- Time-to-first-call (TTFC) median and 90p.
- First-week retention: % of signups making >5 calls.
- Activation funnel conversion: signup -> first call -> second call -> commit (paid plan).
- Average cost per activated developer (CPL scaled by credit usage).

Operational checklist for experiments
---------
- [ ] Implement post-call cost receipt UI in Console (short text + link to billing). (jira:GTMP-482)
- [ ] Add ‘dev-quant’ model to onboarding defaults + explanatory tooltip.
- [ ] Wire starter-credit automated email cadence.
- [ ] Instrument TTFC and funnel events; create dashboard.
- [ ] Prepare 3 landing variants (usage-first, starter-credit, commit-lite) and route 30%/30%/30% + 10% control.

Risks & guardrails
---------
- Overpromising on latency: ensure language says "typical medians for dev-sized requests" not absolute SLAs.
- Starter credits cluttering billing support: create an in-product FAQ and short flow to escalate.
- Commit-lite friction: keep smallest commitment small ($500/mo) to reduce drop-off.

Open questions (for PD/product/legal)
---------
1) Minimum commitment for commit-lite discounts? Suggested = $500/mo.
2) Is promo credit taxable/in region-specific limits? (legal)
3) Which paid tiers get auto-SLA vs manual enable?

Next steps (owners)
---------
- Maya: write landing copy & microcopy variants (due 2025-12-12).
- Samir: instrument TTFC + billing-receipt prototype (due 2025-12-19).
- Ivy: run initial 10% beta on new signups and collect qualitative feedback (due 2026-01-05).

Notes-to-self
---------
Keep language concrete and example-based. Developers respond to small, measurable guarantees (e.g., "expect 200–500ms for hello-world on hosted small payloads") and to visible cost math. Avoid fuzzy descriptors like "cheap" without quick unit examples.

End.
